section_summary.extract_value: This discussion section presents the findings of a single study that investigated the relationships between body image (body appreciation and body dissatisfaction) and subjective happiness in two samples of Western women. The results indicate that body appreciation is a strong positive predictor of subjective happiness, and that body appreciation is influenced by age and BMI. The section also highlights the ubiquity of weight-based dissatisfaction and discusses the limitations of the online, self-selecting survey, including the cross-sectional design and reliance on self-reported data.
section_summary.evidence_source: 4 Discussion Using data from the YBIS, we examined the relationships between body image and subjective happiness in two samples of Western women. Overall, our results indicated that women's body appreciation is a strong positive predictor of their subjective happiness. In turn, body appreciation was associated with respondent age and BMI. The latter variable showed a more complex relationship with subjective happiness: BMI had a direct and positive association with subjective happiness, but was also negatively associated with body appreciation. In short, it might be concluded that women who have more positive body attitudes experience greater global happiness, while body appreciation in turn is influenced by a complex set of factors. Our findings should be considered in light of several limitations. First, because our samples were self-selecting, they should not be considered representative of wider populations. Furthermore, because our survey was conducted online, our sample may be biased toward women with Internet access, who are more affluent (United States Census Bureau 2009), or women who have a higher concern with weight or appearance. Finally, the cross-sectional nature of our study means that, although we have interpreted our data consistent with previous studies, we cannot ascertain the direction of predictive associations with certainty.
